note: The shared profile schema: what a subject can be described by, independent of dataset. A concept is the attribute; its columns are the representations a dataset may hold it in - exact number, band, phrase. Column ids are language-neutral and name the representation; values are phrase-ready strings in the dataset's own language. A profile table may carry only columns declared here plus the claim columns its dataset declares, so two datasets that share a column mean the same thing by it. A concept may declare levels, a common scale for grouping across datasets, and each column how it maps onto them (bins for a number, map for a band); age carries the colleague's four bands. Where the cut points are a research choice not yet made - income - no map is declared and to_levels raises rather than guessing.

columns.gender: the dataset's own label for the respondent's gender

age.description: exact age in years, an integer

age_range.description: an age band as the dataset writes it, e.g. '25–34 let' or '30-44'; only the four common bands map onto the levels

columns.education_level: highest attained education, as a phrase

columns.region: region name, spelled as the reference results spell it
columns.town_size: settlement size band, as a phrase

columns.employment_status: employment status, several joined by commas, as a phrase

columns.income_range: household income band, as a phrase

columns.living_standard: self-assessed living standard, as a phrase

columns.interest_in_politics: interest in politics, as a phrase

columns.opinion_on_eu: satisfaction with EU membership, as a phrase already agreeing with the gender

columns.opinion_on_nato: satisfaction with NATO membership, as a phrase already agreeing with the gender

columns.covid_vaccinated: covid vaccination answer - yes, no or non-substantive - as the dataset writes it
